page.layout: One printed page: a single text column, with a narrow strip of the facing page cut off at the right edge. No running head, margin notes or catchword.

main_text.p: Et cap. Etsi. Etsi damnatis ab homine, aliud est sella terrena, aliud est tribunal cœleste: ab inferiore accipit sententiam, à superiore coronâ. Notatu etiam dignum est, quod legitur cap. Illud plane. Illud plane non temere dixerim, quod si quisquam fidelium fuerit anathemati satus injustè, potius ei oberit qui facit, quàm qui hanc patitur injuriam. Spiritus enim sanctus habitans in sanctis, per quē quisque ligatur aut solvitur, immeritā nulli ingerit poenam. Quæcunq; ergo in nos vibrat pontifex cū suis juratis anathemata, necessum est ut tandem redundent in capita maledicentium: nos interea studebimus inservire Domino Deo nostro ex praescripto verbi prophetici & apostolici, bona conscientiâ. 9 Deum severiore vindicta ulcisci eos, qui ipsius ordinationi resistunt.
Resp. Benedicet autem eis, qui exeunt Româ, quiq; averfantur synagogam pontificiam: quia facta est Babylon, sicuti docuimus antea, & officina omnium scelerum & haeresion.

page.notes: The facing page is only partly visible at the right edge; its text is cut off and not transcribed. Reading of "ulcisci eos" is somewhat uncertain because of the ligature in the print. The final word "seŵn" is printed with a tilde over the w and is set as a hyphenated word split across the lines ("hære-" / "seŵn."). Reading "haeresion" is based on the broken line at the foot of the column.
